bib.title: The Pushshift Reddit Dataset
bib.venue: Proceedings of the Fourteenth International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2020)

question: How can researchers get large-scale historical and real-time Reddit data without the engineering cost of collecting it?
contributions: Release of Pushshift Reddit dataset: monthly dumps of all submissions and comments 2005-2019
A search/aggregation API and a Slackbot for querying and visualising the data
A description aligned with FAIR principles, replacing earlier informal documentation

method.summary: Describes Pushshift's pipeline (ingest engine, PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, API) and the resulting dump of all Reddit submissions and comments, stored as monthly ndjson files with the fields listed in Tables 1 and 2. Dataset paper: no models, no filtering or quality analysis.
method.task: social media dataset release / data infrastructure

datasets.name: Pushshift Reddit dataset
datasets.split: none; one ndjson file per month, June 2005 to April 2019
datasets.source: Reddit API plus scraping, collected by Pushshift since 2015 with historical backfill; users asked to cite Pushshift; full dump is several terabytes

inference.retrieval: Elasticsearch full-text search via API; query size limit five times Reddit's 100-object limit

eval.protocol: Descriptive statistics and a qualitative feature comparison (Table 3); no experiments

results.setup: Reddit, June 2005 to April 2019, Pushshift dump
results.quote: The dataset consists of 651,778,198 submissions and 5,601,331,385 comments posted on 2,888,885 subreddits.
results.note: Intro rounds to 651M submissions and 5.6B comments 'between 2005 and 2019'.

results.claim: By April 2019 the dataset has about 5M comments per day, and over 1M per day after August 2013.

results.quote: After Au- gust 2013, we have consistently over 1M comments per day, while by the end of our dataset (April 2019) we have 5M comments per day.

limits: No analysis of completeness, duplication, deleted content, bots, toxicity or quality; the authors only cite Gaffney and Matias 2018 scrutiny and Baumgartner 2018 response.
Coverage ends April 2019; pre-dates Pushshift's later restrictions.
Not a language-model paper; LM pretraining use appears only as brief mention under 'Robust intelligence'.
Total size in bytes and token count not given.
